rationale:
Issue #901 reports that a Line Separator (U+2028) inside a comment makes dartfmt abort with 'The formatter produced unexpected output', because the formatter trims trailing comment whitespace with String.trim() semantics while its self-check comparison (_isWhitespace in lib/src/string_compare.dart) recognized only ASCII whitespace (0x0009-0x000D, 0x0020). The minimized production patch changes exactly that predicate to the String.trim() set, which is the single behavioral cause of the reported mismatch; the commit message and PR #944 body ('Don't crash when trailing non-ASCII whitespace is trimmed. Fix #901') confirm the same defect. The minimized patch is one hunk in one function plus the doc comment describing that predicate; the unrelated 'library dart_style.src.string_compare;' removal present in the original commit was dropped during minimization, and no test, config, or feature change remains. The triggers are upstream tests from the same fixing commit, not curator-written, and they exercise pre-existing API: test/formatter_test.dart::whitespace unicode.unit formats comments containing U+2028 and the other Unicode whitespace code points end-to-end (the exact reported scenario), and test/string_compare_test.dart::test unicode whitespace characters exercises the already-existing equalIgnoringWhitespace entry point; the fix introduces no new public API. Strict evidence for both original and post-minimization runs passed all gates, with reproduced triggers limited to those two selectors, deterministic across 3 repetitions, buggy full-suite failures confined to the reproduced triggers, and fixed revision all green. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so #901 is not a duplicate, and it matches allowed_root_cause_ids.

Issue #901 reports that a U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR inside a comment makes dartfmt abort with 'The formatter produced unexpected output', where the reported output is the correctly formatted source with the separator removed. That symptom is exactly a disagreement between the trimming dartfmt applies to trailing comment whitespace (String.trim() semantics, Unicode-aware) and the ASCII-only `_isWhitespace` used by the self-check comparison in lib/src/string_compare.dart, which then judged input and output unequal. The minimized production patch changes only that predicate to the String.trim() whitespace set (including 0x2028), and nothing else: the `library dart_style.src.string_compare;` removal present in patches/original-commit.patch is excluded from patches/minimized-production.patch, and the minimized form still passes every strict gate (strict_post_minimization.checks all passed), so the excluded line was cosmetic and non-load-bearing. Triggers come from the same upstream commit, not curator invention. The reproduced ones are test/formatter_test.dart::'whitespace unicode.unit', an end-to-end format of comments containing U+2028 and the other Unicode spaces that matches the reported scenario, and test/string_compare_test.dart::'test unicode whitespace characters', which exercises the pre-existing `equalIgnoringWhitespace` entry point directly. Neither depends on an API introduced by the fix: `equalIgnoringWhitespace` and the .unit fixture runner predate the commit, and the only new test-side code is the `_unescapeUnicode` helper in test/utils.dart, which is test scaffolding for expressing code points in fixtures. The inverted assertion in string_compare_test (isFalse to isTrue) is the removal of an assertion that encoded the buggy ASCII-only assumption, not a feature extension; the independent formatter_test trigger anchors it to the reported defect. Buggy-revision differential and fixed-revision cleanliness are machine-verified in both strict reports (trigger.buggy_differential, trigger.fixed_clean, full_suite.fixed_all_green, 3 repetitions, 56 matrix runs). active_same_project_root_causes is empty and #901 is the sole allowed verified issue key, so no duplicate root cause.

risks: The trigger patch carries two unrelated test-only reformatting edits in test/command_line_test.dart and their selectors are declared as triggers; they do not reproduce the defect (they pass on the buggy revision) but add noise to the trigger set and could be pruned.
test/whitespace/trailing.unit is declared as a trigger but does not reproduce (ASCII-only trailing whitespace), so it contributes no differential signal.

test/string_compare_test.dart inverts a prior assertion from isFalse to isTrue, so on its own it reads as an intentional expectation change; the defect character is established by the end-to-end unicode.unit trigger and the issue report rather than by that assertion.
The predicate drops U+180E relative to the old test list; this matches current String.trim() semantics but is not independently verified by the supplied evidence.
